 Kaante Director Sanjay Gupta Dies After Head Injury
 By REDIFF MOVIES 
 Updated: October 31, 2026 12:32 IST 
 2 Minutes Read 
 Summarize this -->
 Listen to this article 
 Share this Article 
 x 
 'He fell in the kitchen last night and sustained a head injury. Unfortunately, he passed away.' 
 IMAGE: Sanjay Gupta with his wife Anuradha Lekhi, at the screening of Jazbaa in 2015. The film, directed by Gupta, marked Aishwarya Rai's comeback after becoming a mum. Photograph: The late Pradeep Bandekar/Rediff Archives 
 Key Points
 Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta died at his home on October 30 at the age of 57.
 His passing was due to a head injury sustained at home.
 The news was confirmed by fellow filmmaker Ashoke Pandit on X, who expressed shock and sadness.
 Kaante Director Sanjay Gupta died at his home on October 30. He was 57.
 Filmmaker Ashoke Pandit confirmed the news on X: 'It"s really shocking and sad. Just got the news that our dear friend an ace director @_sanjaygupta is no more. He passed due to a head injury at home. Another talent gone too soon. He was a wonderful narrator, full of life persona & a passionate filmmaker. A great loss to our industry. Will miss you my friend. Condolences to his family & dear ones. Om Shaanti.'
 'He fell in the kitchen last night and sustained a head injury. Unfortunately, he passed away. We are in shock,' Sanjay Gupta's close friend Hanif Chunawala shared.
 Sanjay Gupta celebrated his birthday just a few days earlier on October 23.
 An avid biker, Gupta was known for directing and producing films like Mumbai Saga, Kaabil, Shootout At Wadala, Zinda and Kaante .
 He made his directorial debut in 1994 with the star-studded Aatish: Feel the Fire .
 Sanjay Gupta was quite active on social media, particularly on X, where he frequently shared his opinions on various issues concerning the film industry.
 Sanjay Gupta's last film
 On the professional front, his last directorial venture was 2024's The Miranda Brothers , starring Harshvardhan Rane and Meezaan Jafri. As a producer, he also came up with Visfot , featuring Fardeen Khan and Riteish Deshmukh.
 Known for his work in action and crime-based films, Gupta made a significant contribution to Hindi cinema through his distinctive storytelling and films centred on crime, action and drama.
 Gupta is survived by his wife Anuradha Lekhi and their children, Shivansh and Dalai.
 With inputs from ANI.
